=== 0. the constants the loop is written around ===

# A port that changes one of these has changed a derived number, not a name.
# MOST_AT_ONCE and MAX_LISTED are converse.py's and are pinned by r322a4c.
  REMEMBER_TURNS = 12
  MIN_GAP = 3.0
  SPOKE, NOTICED = 'them', 'noticed'
  TURN_OPENS = ('them', 'noticed')
  NOTHING_DONE = 'nothing was done'
  PAST, PLAIN, ING = 0, 1, 2
  VERBS['click'] = ('clicked', 'click', 'clicking')
  VERBS['key'] = ('pressed', 'press', 'pressing')
  VERBS['type'] = ('typed', 'type', 'typing')

=== 1. remember_doing(): four channels, and the tense carries the state ===

# The past tense belongs to `did` and to nothing else; every other line says in
# words that nothing happened, so a reader that ignores the label still cannot
# conclude a click landed. Only `offered` and `turned_down` are fed anywhere in
# measure/, which makes these the least protected sentences in the file.

-- offered --
  [click with a role]
    offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  [click with no role]
    offered | 'to click the thing "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  [type]
    offered | 'to type "hello" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  [key]
    offered | 'to press enter — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  [a kind VERBS does not list]
    offered | 'to press  — nothing was done; they have not accepted'

-- refused --
  [click with a role]
    could not | 'click the button "Copy" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  [click with no role]
    could not | 'click the thing "Copy" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  [type]
    could not | 'type "hello" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  [key]
    could not | 'press enter — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  [a kind VERBS does not list]
    could not | 'press  — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turned_down --
  [click with a role]
    they said no to | 'clicking the button "Copy" — nothing was done'
  [click with no role]
    they said no to | 'clicking the thing "Copy" — nothing was done'
  [type]
    they said no to | 'typing "hello" — nothing was done'
  [key]
    they said no to | 'pressing enter — nothing was done'
  [a kind VERBS does not list]
    they said no to | 'pressing  — nothing was done'

-- did --
# `did` is the one channel handed the widget as it was AT THE MOMENT OF ACTING,
# so its role comes from the world while the other three print the role the
# model chose. Here the model chose `button` and the world says `combo box`.
  [click with a role]
    did | 'clicked the combo box "Copy"'
  [click with no role]
    did | 'clicked the combo box "Copy"'
  [type]
    did | 'typed "hello"'
  [key]
    did | 'pressed enter'
  [a kind VERBS does not list]
    did | 'pressed '

-- the order within one call --
# Source order: offered, did, could not, they said no to. It is not cosmetic —
# converse.still_open() closes every open offer on any settling line, so an
# offer written in the same call as a settlement is already closed by the time
# the next prompt is built.
  offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  did | 'clicked the button "Cut"'
  could not | 'type "bye" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  they said no to | 'pressing tab — nothing was done'

-- nothing to record --
# Four empty channels is the default, so a turn that did nothing writes nothing.
  (empty)

=== 2. recent(): a window measured in turns, cut where a turn opens ===

# A turn opens on `them` or `noticed` and on nothing else. 0 is none and None is
# all: `history[-0:]` was the whole list, so the one value a person reaches for
# to turn memory off used to turn it all the way up.
-- the history being windowed --
  offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'alpha'
  you | 'reply alpha'
  them | 'bravo'
  you | 'reply bravo'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=None -> 12 lines --
  offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'alpha'
  you | 'reply alpha'
  them | 'bravo'
  you | 'reply bravo'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=0 -> 0 lines --
  (empty)

-- turns=-1 -> 0 lines --
  (empty)

-- turns=1 -> 3 lines --
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=2 -> 6 lines --
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=3 -> 9 lines --
  them | 'bravo'
  you | 'reply bravo'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=4 -> 12 lines --
  offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'alpha'
  you | 'reply alpha'
  them | 'bravo'
  you | 'reply bravo'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- turns=99 -> 12 lines --
  offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'alpha'
  you | 'reply alpha'
  them | 'bravo'
  you | 'reply bravo'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"
  you | 'reply charlie'
  offered | 'to click the button "Open" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
  them | 'delta'
  you | 'reply delta'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- a history no turn has opened --
# Lines written before anybody spoke are legitimate: remember_doing() on a fresh
# session produces them. They are carried while they are all there is.
  turns=None -> 2 lines
    offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
    did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  turns=0 -> 0 lines
    (empty)
  turns=1 -> 2 lines
    offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
    did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  turns=12 -> 2 lines
    offered | 'to click the button "Copy" — nothing was done; they have not accepted'
    did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  an empty history, turns=12 -> []

=== 3. the window as decide() hands it over, turn by turn ===

# remember_turns=2. Turn one writes three lines and turn three writes three, so
# a two-turn window is four lines at one boundary and six at another — which is
# the whole reason the unit is turns: the expensive turns are the ones a
# follow-up refers back to, and a line window shrank the memory exactly there.
-- before turn 1 ('line one') --
  (empty)
-- before turn 2 ('line two') --
  them | 'line one'
  you | 'reply one'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
-- before turn 3 ('line three') --
  them | 'line one'
  you | 'reply one'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  them | 'line two'
  you | 'reply two'
-- before turn 4 ('line four') --
  them | 'line two'
  you | 'reply two'
  them | 'line three'
  you | 'reply three'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- the whole history afterwards --
  them | 'line one'
  you | 'reply one'
  did | 'clicked the button "Share"'
  them | 'line two'
  you | 'reply two'
  them | 'line three'
  you | 'reply three'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  them | 'line four'
  you | 'reply four'

-- recent() afterwards -> 5 lines --
  them | 'line three'
  you | 'reply three'
  could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'
  them | 'line four'
  you | 'reply four'

=== 4. find(): the world as it is now, and the role is half of the key ===

# Character Map, measured: a `text` reading 'Font :' sits in front of a `combo
# box` of the same name. The name alone returns the label, the click lands on a
# piece of text and does nothing — indistinguishable from a click that missed.
  find('Font :', 'combo box') -> combo box 'Font :' @ 86,106 321x30 window='Win' centre=(246, 121)
  find('Font :', 'text') -> text 'Font :' @ 34,107 53x20 window='Win' centre=(60, 117)
  find('Font :', '') -> text 'Font :' @ 34,107 53x20 window='Win' centre=(60, 117)
  find('Font :', 'button') -> (none)
  find('Nothing', '') -> (none)
  find('Nothing', 'button') -> (none)
  reads consumed: 7 (one per find, plus the observe)

-- the tiebreak among namesakes of the same role --
# Nearest to where a thing of that role was last seen: a thing moves rather than
# teleporting past its own copies.
  last seen at [(20, 110), (20, 410)], now at [(20, 310), (20, 140)]
  find('Item', 'list item') -> list item 'Item' @ 0,130 40x20 window='Win' centre=(20, 140)

-- the tiebreak with nothing ever seen --
# `find` is public because an interface resolving an action a second way would
# be a second answer, so it has to work before any observe: the fallback is the
# first candidate, not a crash and not None.
  seen=[]
  find('Item', 'list item') -> list item 'Item' @ 0,300 40x20 window='Win' centre=(20, 310)

-- the role filters the candidates, it does not merely break a tie --
# A mutation found this: with the role dropped from the filter the Character Map
# case still passed, because the nearest thing of that role was the right one.
# Only when the chosen thing MOVES does a namesake of another role end up nearer
# to where it used to be, and win.
  find('Item', 'list item') -> list item 'Item' @ 0,320 40x20 window='Win' centre=(20, 330)
  find('Item', '')          -> text 'Item' @ 0,100 40x20 window='Win' centre=(20, 110)

# Three turns on one session: one that acts, one that only speaks, one that does

=== 6. noticing, and the permission that is not in the utterance ===

# An unprompted effect without standing permission is downgraded to speech, not
# refused: the refusal path is conversational, and the default is that way
# because a wrong click has no undo.
-- may_act_unprompted=False --
  n=0
  trigger kind='perceived' asked=False at=1040.000000 text="'Build succeeded' appeared"
  said='빌드 끝났어요. 열까요?'

    noticed | "'Build succeeded' appeared"

# THE OFFER IS NOT WRITTEN DOWN BY THE LOOP. think() records `did` and `refused`
# and nothing else, so a downgraded effect leaves no `offered` line and
# converse.still_open() cannot see it. Only an interface — app.py's proposal
# row — feeds that channel. Recorded here as it stands, not fixed here.

-- an effect nobody caused runs whoever is asking --
# `unprompted` is false when `because` is None, so an effect built by hand is
# not treated as the agent's own idea. That is the permission model's open edge
# and it is written down here rather than argued about.
  did=["key target='' role='' text='enter' because=None unprompted=False | target=(none) | confirmed=None"]
  proposed=[] refused=[]
  hands: ["key 'enter'"]

=== 7. poll(), and the floor a watch keeps ===

# Perception changes 13 seconds in 14 and a model call costs 0.3-2 s, so an
# unfloored watch is a model that never stops and an agent that never listens.
# The clock below is moved by this file; nothing here reads the wall.
  watches: WindowChanged(gap=3.0), Appeared('build'), Vanished('mute')

-- t=1050.000000 (+0.0) : first poll: there is no BEFORE, so nothing whatever happened --
  seen now: ['닫기', 'Share', 'Mute (m)']
  fired: (nothing)

-- t=1050.000000 (+0.0) : the window changed, something appeared, something went away --
  seen now: ['Send', 'Build succeeded']
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1050.000000 text="the window changed to 'Mail'"
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1050.000000 text="'Build succeeded' appeared"
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1050.000000 text="'Mute (m)' went away"

-- t=1051.000000 (+1.0) : all three would fire and all three are inside the floor --
  seen now: ['닫기', 'Build again', 'Mute (m)']
  fired: (nothing)

-- t=1053.500000 (+2.5) : 3.5 s after the LAST FIRING, not 2.5 s after the last check --
  seen now: ['Send', 'Build succeeded']
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1053.500000 text="the window changed to 'Mail'"
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1053.500000 text="'Build succeeded' appeared"
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1053.500000 text="'Mute (m)' went away"

-- t=1056.500000 (+3.0) : exactly at the floor, which is not inside it --
  seen now: ['닫기', 'Build again', 'Mute (m)']
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1056.500000 text="the window changed to 'Win'"
  fired: kind='perceived' asked=False at=1056.500000 text="'Build again' appeared"

-- a session with no watches still looks --
# poll() observes whether or not anything is watching, so `seen` is fresh for
# the next decision. Returning [] because it never looked is a different bug.
  poll() -> []  seen=['닫기', 'Share', 'Mute (m)'] reads=1
  poll() -> []  seen=['Send', 'Build succeeded'] reads=2

=== 8. perform(): resolved against the world AS IT IS NOW ===

# Thirteen times in fourteen, over the second a call takes, something listed when
# the question was asked is gone when the answer arrives. Clicking a remembered
# rectangle is clicking where something used to be.
-- the target moved between the question and the answer --
  n=0
  trigger kind='said' asked=True at=1066.500000 text='close it'
  said='닫을게요'
  n_widgets=4
  look_s=0.125000 think_s=0.250000 act_s=0.250000 total_s=0.625000
  did: click target='닫기' role='button' text='' because=said unprompted=False | target=button '닫기' @ 999,500 40x30 window='Win' centre=(1019, 515) | confirmed=False
  proposed: (none)
  refused: (none)
  hands: ["click button '닫기' at (1019, 515)"]

-- the target had gone by then --
  n=0
  trigger kind='said' asked=True at=1076.500000 text='close it'
  said='닫을게요'
  n_widgets=4
  look_s=0.125000 think_s=0.250000 act_s=0.250000 total_s=0.625000
  did: (none)
  proposed: (none)
  refused: click target='닫기' role='button' text='' because=said unprompted=False
  hands: (nothing)
  blind=0 vanished=1 unknown_keys=0 reads=2
  history:
    them | 'close it'
    you | '닫을게요'
    could not | 'click the button "닫기" — it had gone by then; nothing was done'

-- confirmation asks the widget layer, and only when something was clicked --
# None in a dry run: nothing was clicked, so nothing should have changed, and
# False there would read as a failure that never happened.
  [dry run] confirmed=None target=button '닫기' @ 10,20 40x30 window='Win' centre=(30, 35)
  [still exactly where it was] confirmed=False target=button '닫기' @ 10,20 40x30 window='Win' centre=(30, 35)
  [the thing is gone] confirmed=True target=button '닫기' @ 10,20 40x30 window='Win' centre=(30, 35)
  [the window changed] confirmed=True target=button '닫기' @ 10,20 40x30 window='Win' centre=(30, 35)

-- an effect of a kind perform() has no arm for --
# Refused, not attempted and not raised. converse() cannot build one, so this is
# reachable only by an interface constructing an Intent — which is a thing an
# interface is allowed to do.
  did=["click target='Share' role='button' text='' because=None unprompted=False | target=button 'Share' @ 60,20 40x30 window='Win' centre=(80, 35) | confirmed=False"]
  proposed=[]
  refused=["scroll target='Pane' role='pane' text='' because=None unprompted=False"]
  hands: ["click button 'Share' at (80, 35)"]
# `vanished` counts a target that went, and an unknown kind is not that.
  blind=0 vanished=0 unknown_keys=0 reads=3

=== 9. decide(): a key the environment does not have ===

# The model has emitted {'key': 'zoom in'}, a key on no platform. `press` raises
# and nothing between it and think() catches, so one invented keystroke used to
# cost the whole turn — including the sentence already composed.
-- declares three keys --
  n=0
  trigger kind='said' asked=True at=1126.500000 text='확대해줘'
  said='확대할게요'
  n_widgets=4
  look_s=0.125000 think_s=0.250000 act_s=0.250000 total_s=0.625000
  did: (none)
  proposed: (none)
  refused: (none)
  hands: (nothing)
  blind=1 vanished=0 unknown_keys=1 reads=1
  history:
    them | '확대해줘'
    you | '확대할게요'

-- declares nothing, so keeps every key --
  n=0
  trigger kind='said' asked=True at=1136.500000 text='확대해줘'
  said='확대할게요'
  n_widgets=4
  look_s=0.125000 think_s=0.250000 act_s=0.250000 total_s=0.625000
  did: key target='' role='' text='zoom in' because=said unprompted=False | target=(none) | confirmed=None
  proposed: (none)
  refused: (none)
  hands: ["key 'zoom in'"]
  blind=0 vanished=0 unknown_keys=0 reads=1
  history:
    them | '확대해줘'
    you | '확대할게요'
    did | 'pressed zoom in'

# A dropped key is not filed as something that WENT AWAY: `could not` means it
# had gone by then, and that sentence would be false in the core's own context
# on the very next call.

-- decide() looks first if nothing has been observed --
# A decision needs a world, and the first read is not the interface's job to
# remember. The count is how a port shows it did the same thing.
  before: seen=[] reads=0
  after:  n_seen=4 reads=1 say='ok' effects=[]
  intent.trigger kind='said' asked=True
